activities.caption: drag between bare optics and added optics
activities.name: optLensCompare

config.prompt: Drag across the eye's focusing problem:

before.label: the eye alone
before.text: A living optical instrument that must land focus on the retina across a lifetime — miss by a fraction of a millimetre, roughly a quarter of a dioptre, and the patient notices blur.

after.label: with the spectacle lens
after.text: A carefully ground piece of material pre-bends the light so the eye's own optics finish the job — applied optics with a prescription pad.

config.why: Once the vocabulary — Snell's law, vergence, power, Prentice's rule — is in place, every clinical question becomes one-line arithmetic.

activities.anchor: Because the largest single jump is air to tears
activities.caption: rank the ocular media by refractive index
activities.name: optMediaOrder

config.prompt: Order the ocular media by refractive index, lowest first:
items: tear film and aqueous humour — about 1.336
crystalline lens — about 1.386–1.406 as it accommodates
config.why: The staircase's biggest step is the first one — which is why refractive surgery reshapes the cornea, where the power lives.

activities.anchor: the trial frame's dials are a vergence calculator
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the vergence ledger
activities.name: optVergenceCloze

config.text: Light from a point %%0%% metre away carries −1.00 D; from 25 cm, %%1%% D. Parallel light — practically anything beyond about %%2%% metres — carries zero vergence. And lenses simply %%3%% their power to the incident vergence.
config.hint: Vergence is 1 over the distance in metres — and the lens adds to it.

activities.anchor: the reading-add prescription that nearly every patient meets by midlife
activities.caption: guess the magnitude — the 40 cm bill
activities.name: optAccomEstimate

config.prompt: An emmetrope reads at 40 cm. How much accommodation must the eye add, in dioptres?
config.why: One over the distance in metres: 1/0.40 = +2.50 D. Childhood amplitude runs about 15 D and falls to roughly 2 D by 40 — the reading add arrives when demand meets amplitude.
config.context: amplitude: about 15 D in childhood, roughly 2 D at 40, under 1 D in the fifties

activities.anchor: The retina is fixed and nothing translates
activities.caption: true or false — how the eye focuses
activities.name: optCameraJudge

statements.s: The eye focuses the way a camera does, by moving its lens back and forth.
statements.why: Focus changes entirely by reshaping the crystalline lens — the ciliary muscle slackens the zonules and the elastic lens bulges.

statements.s: A camera changes where its lens sits; the eye changes what its lens is.
statements.why: The one-line summary of the difference.

statements.s: A lens that can no longer bulge is the whole story of presbyopia.
statements.why: When the crystalline lens stiffens, near work blurs — the reading add takes over.

statements.s: The cornea's focusing power is adjustable on demand.
statements.why: The cornea supplies the large, fixed part; the modest, adjustable part is the crystalline lens.

activities.anchor: the classic case for contact lenses, which move with the eye
activities.caption: file each prism as prescribed or smuggled
activities.name: optPrismSort

config.prompt: Deliberate or inadvertent — file each prism:

items.label: base-in, base-out, base-up or base-down to rescue binocular alignment
giving a strabismic patient two images they can fuse without effort
created by Prentice's rule: Δ = c · F
a strong lens read 4 mm off its optical centre
the reason measuring pupillary distance is clinical work, not cosmetics

config.why: The unit is the prism dioptre — 1Δ shifts an image 1 cm sideways at 1 m — and decentration injects it uninvited.

activities.anchor: Tscherning's ellipse is the classic design solution
activities.caption: pair each monochromatic aberration with its signature
activities.name: optAberMatch

config.prompt: The aberrations no eye escapes — pair each with its signature:

pairs.right: peripheral rays of a wide pupil focus in front of central rays — part of night myopia
off-axis point images smear into a comet shape
power errors away from the axis — why spectacle designers choose base curves
pincushion warp for strong plus, barrel warp for strong minus — the goldfish-bowl effect

config.why: Modern wavefront aberrometry measures the whole pattern as higher-order Zernike terms — keratoconic corneas produce spectacular ones.

activities.anchor: one reason acuity falls when the pupil dilates even in an otherwise healthy eye
activities.caption: walk the 20/20 consult
activities.name: optAcuityBranch

config.root: A patient reads 20/20 and demands proof that their optics are perfect. Walk the consult.

choices.label: Resolution of the whole system — aberrations can still ride along

perfect.text: No — acuity is a resolution measurement, and a 20/20 eye can carry substantial higher-order and chromatic error.

resolution.text: And beneath every eye sits a floor. What is it?

choices.label: Diffraction through a 2–3 mm pupil — about one arcminute, the 20/20 letter
None — a perfect eye has no floor

nofloor.text: There is a floor: below three millimetres diffraction blurs, above it aberration does — the optimum sits in between.

done.text: Acuity is a resolution measurement, not an optics certificate — and some sharp young eyes owe part of their edge to small pupils masking aberration.

config.why: Which is also why pinhole apertures can briefly sharpen nearly any refractive error in the examination lane.
